# Working on braid

## Read and resume

Read these instructions explicitly. For initial implementation, read the exact supplied filled assignment packet, worker skill, assigned item, and the packet's read-now context before acting. The packet names relevant sections of `README.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, and the assigned epic/current checkpoint; accepted dependency facts carry exact evidence references. Historical dependency reports are consulted when the task requires re-evaluation or facts conflict, not routinely reread. Verify your actual checkout and your own acceptance evidence independently.

On worker resume, open the named worker checkpoint first, refresh applicable instructions and changed policy, reconcile relevant actual state and interrupted effects, then continue its recorded next action. Do not replay initial discovery. Coordinators read the assigned epic/current checkpoint/items and relevant decisions/dependency evidence to prepare that context. Independent reviewers retain their assigned evidence-reading requirements. Treat current files as the handoff; historical chat and `inspiration/` are supporting context.

For a goal-level planning or orchestration request, use [.agents/skills/braid-coordinate/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/braid-coordinate/SKILL.md). For execution or resumption of one assigned implementation item, use [.agents/skills/braid-worker/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/braid-worker/SKILL.md); consume the filled packet, not the blank [coordinator authoring template](.agents/skills/braid-worker/assets/assignment-packet.md). Do not enter the coordinator workflow. Read the selected skill directly if discovery is unavailable. Independent reviewers follow their separately assigned review and the review conventions below. Routine coding questions need neither workflow. An assignment names its epic and checkpoint. An explicitly supplied standalone scope uses its named context and scoped records without creating an epic or backlog item.

Use the Agile vocabulary in `docs/agile-workflow.md`: epic, optional feature grouping, story, task, spike, backlog, acceptance criteria, Definition of Ready, and Definition of Done. Keep existing backlog IDs stable. The original MVP and inspiration retain historical terminology.

Before assigning a review, read and follow the authoritative [review conventions](docs/agile-workflow.md#review-gates-and-indexing). Item reports, user briefings, and pull-request accounts follow [report format](epics/report-format.md), including its trigger contract. Short progress updates stay short and do not replace an item briefing.

Do only the assigned role and scope. A coordinator asked to deliver an epic may advance its ready backlog items within that scope. Do not dispatch a dependent item whose required human merge is unverified; the [human merge stop](.agents/skills/braid-coordinate/references/delivery.md#human-merge-stop) applies. A worker stops after its assigned item and does not launch agents. Keep one implementation worker at a time. A reviewer is assigned separately after the candidate exists. A planning-only request stops after the reviewable plan.

A new epic uses a pinned named integration branch before planning or dispatch. Item branches start from the accepted epic tip, and their pull requests target that epic. One final epic pull request targets main. Item Done is the human merge into the epic. Epic completion and release stay separate. See [Epic and item branches](.agents/skills/braid-coordinate/references/delivery.md#epic-and-item-branches). Commit a new packet at `epics/<project>/<epic>/assignments/<ID>.md` before the item checkout exists. Historical packets under `reports/` stay as evidence. A top-level item thread watches its own pull request and sends one result; the coordinator dedupes by head. Follow [T3 continuation](.agents/skills/braid-worker/references/t3-continuation.md). Keep that worker prompt short and step-explicit. Watch survival across interruption, unassisted repair, and exactly-once delivery are unproven.

The user explicitly requests top-level T3 threads for assigned tasks, including independent reviews where host rules permit, so each has its own listable identity and can own a PR watch when needed. This is standing authorization within the approved delivery scope; a request to continue carries it forward without another thread-creation question. Provider/model/settings differences alone do not change that requested route. Use a subagent only when the user explicitly selects it or a host rule requires it; explain a required exception rather than silently substituting. This preference does not expand scope, WIP, merge or release authority, or authorize replacing an existing run.

## Providers and roles

These instructions are shared project guidance, regardless of model/provider. Load context according to the role and entry mode above; other Markdown files are not assumed to load automatically. Provider/model/reasoning selection is set in T3, not by this file.

This section is the authoritative provider profile. User preference: Sol High for coordination; Grok 4.7 High with 500K context for implementation and for independent reviews (not Opus). The verified coordination route is Sol High (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `reasoningEffort: high`). The verified T3 implementation route is Cursor model `grok-4.7`, with `target.options` set to `{"reasoning_effort":"high","contextWindow":"500k"}`. Follow host rules for capability checks; do not substitute a different provider/model/settings without authorization. Historical assignments retain the settings actually used.

When a coordinator is assigned, it owns `epic.md` and `checkpoints/current.md`, assigns the selected backlog item, checks evidence, and records the next action. Workers own `checkpoints/<task>.md` and `reports/<task>.md` plus their assigned implementation files. Interpret backlog items' shared-status update instructions as reporting those updates to the coordinator in this mode. Do not have both roles edit the shared checkpoint. Coordinator findings go back to the worker as scoped fixes; the coordinator does not implement product changes in that role.

Separately assigned reviewers own their parent-scoped review report/checkpoint, with exact reviewed revision and findings; the coordinator owns the parent's gate status and triage. Keep a running review's assigned output paths until it returns, then reconcile legacy filenames without restarting the review.

In standalone mode, the assigned agent maintains the epic and current checkpoint itself as previously described. See `docs/agent-handoff.md` for exact role prompts and provider loading references.

## Decisions and implementation

- Project, CLI, and local state directory names are `braid`, `braid`, and `.braid/`. Use them consistently in commands, package `bin`, storage, and checks. See `docs/cli-name.md`. The superseded pre-release directory `.crew/` is not read, written, migrated, or deleted. Do not infer an npm scope from the project name.
- Product CLI and core: modern TypeScript on Node.js, strict checking, compiled JavaScript, one npm package initially.
- Automation and operational scripts: PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`), including substantive logic where useful. Do not replace it merely because it is a shell language.
- Source, PRs, build: GitHub and GitHub Actions.
- Package registry: npm, confirmed by the user. No Forgejo deployment is planned. Tailscale remains available for future private infrastructure. Registry selection does not authorize publishing; npm owner/scope/name and release setup are handled before release.
- Adopt the backlog item/checkpoint/report workflow immediately. Add automation incrementally through the roadmap.
- Choose routine implementation details and ordinary dependencies within the assigned scope; record material choices. Escalate scope expansion, paid services, missing credentials, or changes to acceptance standards.
- Surface user-owned blockers promptly with the exact nonsecret action needed and its impact; workers report them to the coordinator, which includes them in the `You` turn report. Continue independent in-scope work instead of waiting on unrelated release setup. Never request raw secret values in chat.
- Use `rg` for file/text discovery. Keep external command invocation explicit; propagate native exit codes in PowerShell. Avoid shell-interpolated command strings when structured argument lists suffice.

## State, gates, and release discipline

Keep machine state authoritative and human status derived or clearly descriptive. Agents do not hand-edit future `.braid/run.json` files. State and event records must have documented revision and failure behavior; do not claim crash guarantees that have not been tested.

The first release records manual progress. A human/agent marking an item complete is not independent gate evidence. Later gate evidence must identify the exact revision checked.

Run the meaningful checks required by the backlog item. Report commands and results honestly, including checks that could not run. Never weaken a gate or delete a failing test simply to pass. Fixes to an incorrect test or gate require a documented reason and preserved acceptance intent.

`npm run verify` is the deterministic offline pre-PR gate for code and docs. It keeps the OIDC release check, install-policy check, typecheck, build, test, and packed-install steps, and it checks tracked Markdown relative links and heading anchors (not `inspiration/` or external URLs) and tracked-text LF endings and trailing whitespace. External skill validators are not part of that command. Run them when a change edits skill content and report them separately; they may be unavailable in CI.

Develop future versions under a pinned, released controller installed outside the candidate checkout. Record controller version and schema version; do not upgrade active runs silently.

## Shared and external actions

Respect user changes. Inspect git status before editing. Work only in the assigned checkout and branch. A scoped delivery request authorizes scoped Conventional Commits, pushes to an owned feature branch, and PR creation after relevant local gates pass; follow `.agents/skills/braid-coordinate/references/delivery.md`. Human merge authority remains unchanged. Green CI and independent review are not a merge. When later work requires one, stop at the [human merge stop](.agents/skills/braid-coordinate/references/delivery.md#human-merge-stop). Do not create a remote repository, merge, publish a release/package, deploy infrastructure, or change tailnet policy unless the task authorizes that action.

Spikes also deliver through PR, applicable CI, and review. Local acceptance is distinct from Done after CI/review/approved merge. Preserve existing user commits/index, and do not stage/commit/switch a shared checkout while a worker is running. Workers follow their assigned Git boundaries; the coordinator handles a Git transition only at a safe handoff boundary.

README is the repository frontend for supported capabilities, setup, usage, architecture, and limits. Keep current backlog/progress and handoff details in the epic/checkpoints/reports. A stable link to contributor documentation is fine; do not use README as a coordinator dashboard.

Do not put secrets in chat, git, reports, fixtures, or logs. Reference secret names and use the environment's secret mechanism when needed. Do not copy permissions or infrastructure identities from `inspiration/`.

## Checkpoint and finish

At a useful boundary, before switching context, and before ending a task, apply [Commit boundary](docs/agile-workflow.md#commit-boundary): workers update record files before push; afterward report checks and blockers in the PR comment and result message without editing those files.

1. Update the owned checkpoint (`checkpoints/<task>.md` for a coordinated worker, `checkpoints/current.md` for the coordinator or standalone agent): task, checkout/branch/HEAD when available, completed work, in-flight commands, next concrete action, blockers, checks, and changed files. The coordinator rewrites `checkpoints/current.md` and appends `checkpoints/log.md` ([Now and the log](docs/agile-workflow.md#now-and-the-log)).
2. Coordinator/standalone agent: update the assigned row in `epic.md` with status and evidence/report links. Coordinated workers return proposed status updates in their report.
3. Write `reports/<task>.md` using [report format](epics/report-format.md). Review passes use the parent-scoped report convention. Distinguish local proof from remote CI/release proof.
4. At an item outcome, a user-attention blocker, a substantive child return, or a milestone, give the user that same account. Keep routine progress concise. If blocked, name the exact input that unblocks the work and continue independent in-scope work.

The checkpoint should let a fresh agent resume without the conversation.

# Braid worker

Complete only the assigned item. Make routine in-scope choices; do not launch agents, schedule successors, run a coordinator loop, or award independent approval/Done.

## Initial entry: context and checkout

Use the shared [workflow map](../../../docs/directory-structure.md) only for Braid records. Target layout, architecture and checks come from project instructions and the approved brief, not Braid's repository. Workflow links resolve in the skill installation; project-context paths resolve in the target checkout.

Open the exact supplied filled-packet path; do not search for it or routinely load the blank [coordinator authoring template](assets/assignment-packet.md). Read applicable target-project instructions, this skill, the assigned item and read-now context once; assignment paths override global pointers. Keep a short read index. These skills cannot waive another project's mandatory instructions; unresolved conflicts go back to the coordinator before affected actions.

Use the packet's separate read-now context, verified dependency facts with exact evidence references, and on-demand history. Accept recorded dependency/merge facts unless inputs change or evidence contradicts them; independently verify your checkout and your own acceptance evidence. Required context must be committed or explicitly supplied, not dependent on parent chat/dirty files/ignored inspiration. Historical reports support re-evaluation when needed, not routine startup.

Use singular authorities: [Agile workflow](../../../docs/agile-workflow.md) for Ready/Done/review; [delivery rules](../braid-coordinate/references/delivery.md) for Git and green-only handoff; [report format](../../../epics/report-format.md) for reports/PRs. Load relevant sections as needed. Legacy wording cannot permit failed handoff.

Require scope, dependency/merge evidence, Git/ownership contract, outputs, check set and supported continuation. Report missing facts and impact to the coordinator; continue independent work. The packet cannot weaken acceptance or host restrictions.

In one batch compare host-bound root, status/staged index, full HEAD, branch, origin and expected upstream state against the packet. A new branch without upstream is normal when declared; use the explicit first push destination. A match needs no routine fetch, upstream repair, history or branch inventory: perform the packet's concrete first useful action. Stay on the packet's named item branch, started from the accepted epic tip. Retain a generated branch only when the packet explicitly assigns that legacy route. On the initial batch, a missing checkout, a detached HEAD, or a branch or head that differs from the packet stops the affected writes. Never create child worktrees in the shell, guess a path, rename the bound branch, or repair the binding. Preserve unexpected changes/index; reconcile only the mismatch before affected actions. No reset/clean, silent base switch/rebase or force-push. Authorized base changes invalidate affected proof.

## Resumed entry: checkpoint first

Open the named worker checkpoint first to recover phase, ownership, existing PR/head, continuation generation and next action. Refresh applicable instructions and changed policy as needed. Before side effects, reconcile only relevant actual Git/PR/check/process/task/transport state, including whether interrupted commit/push/PR/check operations completed. Reuse the existing branch/PR and valid proof; continue the recorded action without replaying the original implementation prompt or architecture research.

Reconcile stale/duplicate events by current head/run/attempt; record observed state and explicit task lineage. Do not assume a subscription or process survived, create another PR, or repeat readiness registration without a demonstrated need. Concrete contradictions, changed dependencies and high-risk ambiguity still warrant investigation before affected work.

Naturally observed repeated apparent final/yield responses while the same host run stays active and its intended continuation remains queued are a host/transport blocker, not ordinary pending CI. Preserve state, send one explicit blocker through the assigned return channel, report it and stop ordinary execution under host rules; do not replay startup or add readiness generations. For T3 use [stalled yield recovery](references/t3-continuation.md#stalled-yield-recovery).

## Execute first; investigate incrementally

Treat the coordinator's approved brief as the implementation plan. Reopen architecture only for concrete contradictions, missing decisions or risk uncovered by evidence; report material changes before dependent work.

After mandatory context and checkout checks, take the smallest meaningful action: inspect the named function, run a targeted test, reproduce the issue or make a bounded edit. Use a short internal plan for well-defined work, not a second planning deliverable.

- Simple known change: inspect, edit, check. Specified CLI command: inspect adjacent patterns, make a short plan, implement and test. Unfamiliar crash/recovery behavior: investigate alternatives and failure modes before changing the protocol.
- Search named paths/symbols with `rg`; read relevant sections before whole files/directories. Expand only when findings justify it. Batch independent operations and request only relevant diffs, logs and failures.
- Reuse facts already read. Reinspect only for a new question, changed state or required revision verification. If investigation yields no actionable finding, decide whether enough is known to act; further exploration needs a concrete question affecting correctness or proof. No rigid time/tool limits.

## Implement and prove the item

Stay within assigned ownership. Coordinator owns shared epic/status and scheduling; worker owns implementation and item report/checkpoint. Report scope/resource conflicts without blocking independent work. Follow AGENTS security/resource boundaries: no merge/publish/deploy/account/tailnet changes; obtain secrets only through the host mechanism, never chat or evidence.

Reuse the pinned toolchain; install missing dependencies by documented routes. Released controllers stay pinned outside the candidate checkout; record controller/schema versions, never silently upgrade active runs. Use focused development checks, then all required local gates. For this repository, `npm run verify` is the deterministic offline pre-PR gate for code and docs. Run it before opening the pull request. External skill validators stay separate: when a change edits skill content, run them and report that result on its own, including when they are unavailable in CI. Add meaningful regressions when warranted; skill/docs changes need structural/link/scenario proof, not tests matching prose.

Record commands, exit codes, versions and revision; distinguish dirty probes, clean checks, installed-artifact proof and hosted CI. Never weaken a gate, delete failing tests to pass or inherit failure waivers. Repeat passed expensive checks only for relevant changes, failures or unresolved concerns.

## Deliver through green checks

After local gates pass, inspect the scoped diff/index, stage only owned paths, make coherent Conventional Commits and push explicitly to the assigned remote and owned branch (for example `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<owned-branch>`). Create one PR against the assigned base and immediately call the host's PR-link tool as the next call; also link after a later push. Write the PR body with the [human account and technical record](../../../epics/report-format.md#pull-request-records), including when `--body-file` bypasses the repository template. Preserve real dependency ordering. Do not treat an unmerged prerequisite as merged, and do not start a successor. Reuse an existing assigned PR on resume.

Before waiting, include actual root/branch/full HEAD/PR and the frozen check set in the return message. Require a supported host continuation; for T3 read [t3-continuation.md](references/t3-continuation.md) before PR waiting. A top-level item thread links its pull request and watches it, then runs the one catch-up snapshot in that reference. If every declared check has already finished, verify and deliver in that same turn; otherwise end the turn. One watch wake drives verification and a single result to the coordinator. A delegated child does not watch or poll; the legacy parent relay applies only when the packet explicitly selects it. Other hosts need their own supported mechanism supplied or a precise transport blocker, not an invented direct CI wait. No polling loops, schedulers, or background watchers.

Retain item ownership while checks are pending or blocked, even when a conversational turn/task ends. These returns are **nonterminal progress**, never successful handoff. On a failure wake/resume, independently inspect current PR/head, exact run/attempt/job/step logs and scope. Repair in-scope causes yourself, run relevant local gates, commit/push/link and wait for new-head proof. The coordinator dedupes results by head and does not inherit repair ownership. No blind retries; a diagnosed transient rerun needs appropriate authority and a recorded reason. Do not send another result for a head already reported.

On a real event or explicit reconciliation, verify **every check the packet declares** independently: actual PR head, workflow/event/run/attempt/job identities, successful conclusions, and required steps and uploads, including artifact digest and provenance when the packet declares them. A packet may explicitly declare artifact verification not required (for example a docs-only change); the report then says so. PR merge-test source can differ from PR head; preserve both and verify their relationship. Branch protection or a "checks passed" hint cannot shrink the packet's check set. Pending, failed, missing, skipped, cancelled, neutral, inaccessible, inconclusive or stale evidence never silently counts green. Reconfirm current head after proof before handoff. When the target checkout provides `scripts/Test-PrProof.ps1`, produce this proof by running that command. It is a finite snapshot: one `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `PENDING` line plus JSON, and it exits 0 only for `PASS`. Full artifact mode is the default. Pass `-SkipArtifacts` only when the packet explicitly waives artifact verification; the JSON records that limitation, and a download or proof failure never selects the switch. The prose check set above remains the definition. The command is outside `npm run verify` and does not watch or poll. Accept a PASS for an active pull request only when `proofScope` is `current` and the final view is still open on the same target ref. A historical PASS is a merged snapshot and is not current readiness. Every added commit, including docs or evidence, invalidates old-head hosted proof. Record files after that push follow [Commit boundary](../../../docs/agile-workflow.md#commit-boundary).

For infrastructure, access, trigger, transport or out-of-scope failure: preserve diagnostics and state; promptly report exact nonsecret owner/action/impact and a resume action. Continue useful independent work; if none remains, yield blocked under host rules without abandoning ownership or claiming completion. Post-push blockers use the PR comment and result, without editing committed records ([Commit boundary](../../../docs/agile-workflow.md#commit-boundary)).

## Checkpoint, resume and return

Update the owned checkpoint before the push that publishes it. A later update belongs only in a repair commit ([Commit boundary](../../../docs/agile-workflow.md#commit-boundary)). Keep it actionable: task/scope; actual root/branch/full HEAD and dirty/index ownership; read index; changed paths; PR/current checks and proof; controller/schema if applicable; live task/process handles and log locations; unresolved findings/blockers; one exact next action. Put detail in the report, not a second transcript. Do not checkpoint every read or assume a process survives restart.

Use the resumed-entry procedure above after continuation or context replacement; fewer history reads never reduce required current-head checks. If this run already sent the result for the current head, stop without sending another. A repeated reading of the launch prompt inside the same run is not a new assignment. The launch prompt stays short and step-explicit; do not expand it into a resume narrative.

Successful green return follows [report format](../../../epics/report-format.md#human-account): opening, What changed, Why, Left for you, and Technical record. Include decisions, changed outputs, local and hosted evidence, limits, actual root, branch, full head, PR and run links, and the exact next coordinator action. Propose shared-status updates instead of editing files the coordinator writes ([Record ownership](../../../docs/agile-workflow.md#record-ownership)). Green means ready for coordinator acceptance and independent review. Review, triage, human-approved merge, and Done remain separate. Later assigned scoped fixes follow the same green rule. Stop after the item.
